articles.title: Russo-Ukrainian war, day 1679: Russia raises its war budget by 27% to a record as it looks to grow its war in 2027
articles.body:
Exclusives
Military
Russia drained the Kakhovka Reservoir. Now it hides in the dry bed to creep toward Zaporizhzhia. A frontline commander expects small Russian groups to slip into the city by winter. A leading analyst calls that far too categorical—and says the front is moving the other way.
Vivaldi counteroffensive advanced after Ukraine took Russia’s drones out of the fight, ISW assesses. Armored vehicles reached heavy Russian fortifications in the Lyman sector without coming under drone attack, which the analysts read as a sign of Ukrainian drone overmatch.
Russia’s mass drone attacks on Ukraine have a goal—likely Ukraine’s capitulation by spring 2027, ISW says. Until his new theory of victory has played out, Putin is unlikely to soften his demands or enter serious ceasefire talks, according to ISW.
Russia’s pipeline into Kupiansk is now its escape route—with kidnapped civilians as human shields, Ukraine says. Ukrainian drones filmed the column on 27 September. Khartia warned Russia could pass the footage off as an "evacuation" or "rescue" of civilians.
Ukraine makes local gains on Pokrovsk front despite sustained Russian attacks. The marines cleared 5 square kilometers and captured two Russian soldiers.
A Ukrainian Hornet drone hit a Russian radar 120 km behind the front. It was likely a $100 million Nebo-M. The strike is part of a push to cut Russian logistics and strip Russian forces of radar and electronic warfare systems, a brigade officer says.
Ukraine hits railways of Bryansk, Russia’s launchpad for strikes on Kyiv: downed bridge and 28 derailed cars, region’s governor says. Ukraine's drones reportedly hit the region's railways.
Intelligence and technology
Mavic vs Slavic: Ukrainian developers adapt reconnaissance drones to the modern battlefield. “The drone was developed as a Ukrainian alternative to Chinese commercial quadcopters,” Vyriy Industries said.
A Ukrainian firm now rents out drone jammers by the day—but the deposit is the device’s full price. The daily fee comes off a deposit worth the whole device—rent long enough and the jammer becomes yours.
Ukraine just caught a Geran-5 at 425 km/h—the jet drone that has often outrun Ukrainian interceptor drones since January. Ukrainian crews now stop just over half of Russia's jet-powered drones, against more than 90% of the older Shaheds, even as Moscow builds them by the thousand.
Russia is stepping up fake Ukrainian government pages as bait for recruiting agents, Ukraine’s security service says. Russian intelligence uses the counterfeits to spread disinformation and to harvest data on the Ukrainians who subscribe.
Russia is launching a faster Geran-5 at Ukraine that satellite jamming may no longer knock off course, a monitoring channel says. The drone can steer by images of the terrain below, and its extra speed makes it harder for interceptors to catch, though Ukrainian officials have not confirmed the system.
International
Russia ordered arson attack on Estonian military robot-maker supplying Ukraine, Estonia confirms. Estonia says its intelligence service established that Russia’s special services ordered the August fire at Milrem Robotics, as Russian sabotage operations spreads across Europe.
Belgium rushes three F-16s to Ukraine as Russia expands its drone and missile assault. Zelenskyy says the aircraft will arrive by the end of 2026, strengthening Ukraine’s ability to intercept Russian air targets and conduct combat missions.
Russian jet-powered drone hits near Yahodyn, just 1.5 km from Poland, as Warsaw changes air defense rules. Poland plans to allow decisions to engage aerial targets based on radar data.
Lithuania gets its US tank battalion back while the Pentagon weighs pulling up to 40,000 troops from Europe. The Lithuanian leader calls the decision an encouragement and says fewer American soldiers will remain on the continent overall.
Humanitarian and social impact
Russian troops enter homes and threaten starving Oleshky residents for food and alcohol, officials say. Residents who escaped the occupied Kherson Oblast city describe threats and abuse by Russian troops amid severe shortages of food, water, and medicine.
Russian mercenaries blew off African prisoners’ legs to practice battlefield medicine, Wagner fighter says. A Russian mercenary captured by Ukraine describes alleged Wagner training sessions where prisoners were deliberately maimed and killed so recruits could practice battlefield medicine and killing techniques.
Russia hits a Kharkiv high-rise overnight, injuring 43 people, then kills four in daylight strikes on central Kyiv and Dnipro. A pre-dawn strike on Ukraine's second city gave way to drone attacks on a business center and then a national science institution during working hours.
Political and legal developments
Russia raises its war budget by 27% and expands the army again – both to new records – even as its budget deficit widens and oil revenues fall. Moscow plans to spend a record 17.1 trillion rubles on defense in 2027 as it raises taxes and borrowing to cover a widening deficit.
The Kremlin calls mobilization talk “nonsense”—Zelenskyy says it has already begun, with North Korean reinforcements. The claim comes from Ukraine's military intelligence, which has tracked Russian preparations for a larger call-up for months.
War is costing Ukraine $155 billion per year. With Western aid running late, Kyiv is freezing everything but army, pensions, and public wages. Kyiv froze parks, fountains, and road repairs to pay its army and pensioners first.
After Russia hits Kyiv’s Academy of Sciences with jet-powered drone, the Kremlin says Ukraine must “pay a price”. Peskov calls Russia's intensified strikes part of that price.

articles.title: Multiple Explosions Rock Kyiv as Russia Launches Early Morning Missile-and-Drone Assault
articles.body:
Kyiv came under a fresh Russian missile-and-drone attack early Wednesday, Sept. 30, with multiple ballistic missiles targeting the Ukrainian capital as explosions echoed across the city and air defenses engaged incoming threats.
Ukraine’s Air Force warned of an incoming ballistic threat before reporting “ballistic missiles on Kyiv.” Two minutes later came another urgent alert: “More ballistic missiles on Kyiv.”
JOIN US ON TELEGRAM
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
A Kyiv Post journalist in the capital described the assault as it unfolded.
“Kyiv is currently under a ballistic attack. I’ve heard a few loud explosions and several thuds so far. I just saw flashes from the active air defense operations outside my window,” she reported.
Kyiv authorities later reported that at least one woman was wounded in the attack as fires broke out at multiple impact sites across three districts of the capital.
In the Sviatoshynskyi district, private residential buildings caught fire following a Russian strike. A warehouse building was burning in Holosiivskyi, while a shop caught fire in Obolonskyi, according to the Kyiv City Military Administration and Mayor Vitali Klitschko.
Emergency crews were dispatched to the affected areas as air defenses continued operating over Kyiv.
A rapidly escalating aerial blitz
The new assault came only hours after President Volodymyr Zelensky said Russia had launched more than 100 drones against Ukraine during Tuesday alone.
Zelensky Approves October Long-Range Operations, Promises F-16 Reinforcements
Twenty-nine were high-speed jet-powered UAVs, with Ukrainian forces intercepting 18 of them, according to Zelensky.
Ukrainian Air Force spokesperson Yurii Ihnat said Russia used more than 2,800 jet-powered drones during August, compared with far lower numbers earlier in the summer. Their interception rate has been only slightly above 60%, compared with roughly 90-95% for slower piston-engine UAVs.
Capital under relentless attack
Kyiv has endured repeated Russian attacks over the preceding 48 hours.
Overnight into Tuesday, Moscow launched a Zircon/Oniks missile, two Iskander-M/S-400 ballistic missiles and 152 drones against Ukraine, including 82 jet-powered UAVs.
Ukraine’s Air Force said it shot down or suppressed all three missiles and 106 drones – 109 targets in total.
Russian weapons nevertheless struck 24 locations across Ukraine, while debris from intercepted targets fell at another 16 locations.
In Kyiv, the attack damaged residential and non-residential buildings and an educational facility. Fires broke out in several districts, while a drone strike on a six-story residential building injured at least one person.
That barrage followed a deadly daytime attack Monday, Sept. 28, when a high-speed Russian drone slammed into the National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine in central Kyiv during working hours.
The strike on one of Ukraine’s leading scientific institutions came as Russia increasingly targets Kyiv during daylight hours with faster jet-powered drones, creating an almost continuous air threat for civilians in the capital.
Devastation across Ukraine
Russia’s escalating aerial campaign has inflicted casualties far beyond Kyiv.
Earlier Tuesday, Russian forces struck Sumy with four guided aerial bombs. One bomb hit a school while children were inside. Students and teachers had taken shelter and escaped injury, according to Zelensky.
A separate strike hit a residential building. Local authorities later reported two people killed and nine wounded.
In Zaporizhzhia and the surrounding region, Russian attacks wounded 34 people over the previous day. Thirty-three of them were injured when Russian forces struck an industrial facility.
Russian strikes in Odesa also damaged civilian infrastructure, housing, a school and an animal shelter. Six people were reported wounded in the overnight attack.
Patriot supplies under growing pressure
The sustained multi-axis attacks are placing enormous pressure on Ukraine’s air-defense network.
Patriot remains Ukraine’s principal system capable of reliably intercepting Russian ballistic missiles, but supplies of the advanced interceptors are under severe strain.
US Patriot missile stocks in Europe have reached what American and NATO officials described to the Associated Press as a “beyond critical” level, amid competing global requirements for the weapons.
Zelensky said Tuesday that Kyiv continues pressing its partners for additional Patriot missiles.
Ukraine has meanwhile received a new package of missiles for its NASAMS systems, while Belgium will provide three additional F-16 fighter jets before the end of the year. Ukrainian combat aircraft are already being used to destroy Russian attack drones.
Kyiv is also racing to develop its own high-speed interceptor drones capable of hunting Russia’s newer jet-powered UAVs.
Zelensky said Ukrainian interceptors are already being tested and used in combat.
Ukraine has set new production targets for October as developers, manufacturers and the military work to increase interception rates and expand deployment.
Systematic strikes on civilians condemned as war crimes
The deliberate and systematic targeting of civilian infrastructure – including schools, research institutions, residential blocks, and shelters – has drawn renewed condemnation from international legal bodies and human rights organizations, who reiterate that such actions constitute war crimes under international law.
As emergency crews continue clearing wreckage and treating casualties, Kyiv maintains that protecting civilians requires not only intercepting incoming weapons but reducing Russia’s capacity to launch them in the first place.
